description: Mohamed ElSaadani, Emad Habib and Mohamed M. Morsy publish a reproducibility package for comparing flood exposure and structure damage in Louisiana's Vermilion River Basin. The study contrasts NOAA Atlas 14 design storms with stochastic storm transposition scenarios. Its September 2026 archive contains Python analysis code, a dependency list, fifty rainfall realisations and diagnostics covering inundation depths, structure damage, spatial density and Height Above Nearest Drainage. The code is free under MIT; rainfall data, diagnostics and configuration use CC BY 4.0. Scenario duration and spatial resolution remain unknown from the landing page. The documented outputs support comparison of alternative flood-risk simulations, but the metadata do not quantify the resulting differences or establish that every upstream inundation input is included. No related catalogue record is explicitly identified. The associated preprint is the citation, while the Zenodo package is the reusable resource.
